capability.note: drawing and datasheet - 9001-22312 FUNCTIONALITY: CURRENT, POWER, AND ENERGY METERING FOR INPUT AND OUTLET; CURRENT METERING FOR BRANCH; OUTLET SWITCHING. That is the G4 guide's Managed (MA) row of Table 1, so `metering-scope: outlet` and `outlet-switching: true`, the published class `managed` (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 2.2), and every outlet declares `[on, off]`. ON EACH OUTLET'S PLACEMENT, NOT ON THE `outlets` GROUP: the build applies a host group's `states` to whatever is seated in it, so the kit declines to seat a cord end in a slot whose group carries them (render.cage_entries `group-states`, pinned at zero by test_cage_accepts), and the 24 C13s are slots for a C14 cord end. The SKU page's OUTLET CONTROL: No contradicts the drawing and the product name (gaps: outlet-control).

chassis.note: drawing - 9001-22312 MECHANICAL: 72.01 in (1829 mm) length, 2.05 in (52 mm) width, 2.56 in (65 mm) depth, aluminium chassis, black. The 65 is the end cap from the face to the back (582.69 to 656.39 pt on the side view); the outlet mouldings stand 3.96 off the face, their lamps 5.0, the breaker plates 7.54, the network module about 11 and the buttons 9.36 off the back, none of it in the 65. The SKU page's PRODUCT HEIGHT 72 in, WIDTH 2.56 in and LENGTH/DEPTH 2.05 in say the same with the axes renamed (COVERAGE: the page's axis labels are wrong). Weight 28.2 lb (12.8 kg) is the SKU page's.

colours.note: photo-measured - the section colours are the pilot's, the modal saturated pixels of the EVMI2130X outlet bank masters, a FIELD on the strip and breaker parts that each placement sets; CHASSIS_424_HRZ shows the same yellow, blue and orange on D, E and F as on A, B and C. The body is the pilot's #2e3033.

dcim.note: the input is one `cs8365c` power port (eaton/g4-cord-cs8365c@1) and each outlet a power outlet fed by it, `iec-60320-c13` or `eaton-c39`. EACH OUTLET RUNS `through` ITS SECTION'S BREAKER, a fixed part, and each breaker states the `lines` it is across, so the export writes "Through breaker A, lines L1-L2" on each outlet, naming the breaker by its printed letter. NO feed_leg IS WRITTEN: a delta input has no neutral, so every outlet is line to line (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 5.2). THE OUTLETS ARE NAMED AS THE UNIT PRINTS THEM, A1 to F42, through the `interfaces:` rules, as the pilot's are.

ends.note: drawing - the end view of 9001-22312 is the cord end: a grommet 36.9 across, centred on the width and 24.5 behind the face (40.5 from the back), with a toothed strain-relief clamp in a 30.1 bore. Top and bottom views have y = 0 at the rear. No view draws the far end; it is drawn as its end cap alone.

front.note: drawing - the front view of 9001-22312, read in drawing mm (x from the cord end, y from the edge drawn at the top). Six outlet mouldings 181.3 long by 36.0 (y 6.04 to 42.06) start at x 195.09, 444.19, 693.29, 1137.39, 1386.49 and 1635.59, a 249.10 period on each side of the module; each carries seven outlets at the pilot's offsets (a C13 recess 3.24, 54.04, 104.84 and 155.64 into the moulding, a C39 26.54, 77.34 and 128.14) and a printed strip at y 45.5 to 49.5 from 0.51 in. Each section has its breaker plate (60.0 by 48.0, y 2.0 to 50.0) 3.89 before its moulding, at 131.2, 380.3, 629.4, 1073.5, 1322.6 and 1571.7. The network module's faceplate spans 879.45 to 1067.35 and y 1.45 to 50.55, the pilot's 187.9 by 49.1, with its jacks, USB-C, LCD and keys at the pilot's offsets within it (the jack pair centred 36.74 in against the pilot's 36.70). At the cord end, an M6 ground screw (12.5 across at 52.0, 38.0), a screw 6.0 across at 14.0, 26.0 and a round boss 8.2 across at 92.0, 36.0; a second 6.0 screw at 1822.0, 26.0. End caps 2 thick at both ends.

input.note: drawing and datasheet - a CS8365C plug on a fixed 10 ft cord, 6 AWG and four conductors (9001-22312 INPUT). INPUT RATING 200-240V~ DELTA, 3W+PE, 40A, 50/60HZ, so `input-phase: three`, `input-wiring: delta` and `input-voltage-v: 208`, the SKU title's and the SKU page's INPUT VOLTAGE 208V, line to line. The SKU title's 50A is the plug's rating (CS8365C, 50 A 250 V); the drawing's 40A, the SKU page's AMPERAGE RATING 40A, is the derated input. 14.4 kW is the SKU title's and is 40 A x 208 V x root 3 (14.41).

lamps.note: drawing, datasheet and photo - 9001-22312 draws a bump 4.0 by 2.94 on the moulding's outer edge at the far end of every outlet, 42 in all, centred 2.2 to 2.3 before the outlet recess ends (x 218.13 for A1 to 1811.04 for F42). The G4 guide 1.3 gives Metered Outlet, Switched and Managed models an LED per outlet, and the G4 brochure BR155056EN says green indicates power on and red power off to the outlet. Each is eaton/g4-outlet-led@1 placed with `for:` naming its outlet, so a state set on the outlet reaches its lamp (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2); the `outlet-leds` group states the two colours once. CHASSIS_424_HRZ shows them unlit, clear domes over the dark moulding. With no state set a lamp draws unlit, whatever its declared `off`.

left.note: estimated - no view draws the other long side. It is drawn as the right side mirrored front to back, as the pilot's is; CHASSIS_424_SIDE does not resolve the fasteners.

lifecycle.note: no end-of-life notice is held for this SKU; the drawing's first issue is 18-Aug-2023 and the SKU page (generated 2026) lists it as current. The G4 grid lists an EOL notification under a /secure/ path, which was not fetched.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE VENDOR'S VECTOR DRAWING. Eaton drawing 9001-22312 (EVMA8365X G4 MANAGED, first issue 18-Aug-2023, D size, SCALE 0.400) draws the PDU lying down, cord end at the left, in a front view, a side view below it and a rear view below that, with an end view of the cord end, the plug, an isometric and a one-line diagram. Its views are paths, not a raster, so every position here was read off the PDF's geometry with PyMuPDF at 1.133858 pt per mm (0.4 x 72 / 25.4), the way the EVMI2130X was read off 9001-22301. The check on that scale is the drawing's own dimensions: 1829 overall lands at 2073.83 pt (1829.0), the 65.00 depth of the end cap at 73.70 pt (65.0), the buttons at 124.0 and 1679.8 (1555.8 apart) and the holes 55.80 beyond each, all within 0.05. The library draws the PDU STANDING, cord end down, as the pilot does, so a drawing x along the length becomes 1829 minus that, and a drawing y across becomes x. The one-line diagram is the one raster on the sheet (a 504 x 488 JPEG at 96 ppi), read at zoom.

module.note: drawing - the network module is eaton/g4-enmc@1, in a bay, as on the pilot. Read against this drawing as the design note asked: 9001-22312 COMMUNICATION lists G4 eNMC, DUAL GIGABIT ETHERNET WITH NETWORK CASCADING, POWER REDUNDANCY PORT, EMP PORT, 2xUSB-C, MENU PIXEL LCD, which is the part's list, and the faceplate draws PDU+1 and SENSOR, the 0 and 1 network jacks, USB/0 and USB/1, the LCD and four keys (<, >, ESC, enter) at the same offsets in a faceplate of the same 187.9 by 49.1.

mount.note: `rack-side`, as the EVMI2130X: the part stands vertically beside the rack's opening, takes no rack unit and exports u_height 0 and is_full_depth false (docs/vertical-cable-managers-design.md). The G4 installation and setup guide P-164001156 rev 3 hangs every 0U G4 on its two factory buttons in keyhole slots (2.11.2), one or two a side (2.9, Fig. 7). `ru: 41` is the SKU title's 41U; 1829 is 41.1 units. No ears: a 0U PDU has none.

one-line.note: drawing - READ AT ZOOM. 9001-22312's one-line diagram (a raster, re-rendered at 300 dpi) draws L1, L2 and L3 each through a metering element to a vertical bus, the L1 bus leftmost, then L2, then L3, each bus starting at the dot where its line arrives and running down past the crossings it hops. Each breaker is a two-pole switch with an upper and a lower pole. A: the upper pole on L1's line, the lower from the L2 bus's top corner. B: upper on L2 (dot on the L2 bus), lower from the L3 bus's top corner. C: upper on L3 (dot on the L3 bus), lower from a dot on the L1 bus. D: upper from a dot on the L1 bus, lower from a dot on the L2 bus. E: upper from the L2 bus's bottom corner, lower from a dot on the L3 bus. F: upper from the L3 bus's bottom corner, lower from the L1 bus's bottom corner. So A and D are across L1-L2, B and E across L2-L3, and C and F across L3-L1 - the pilot's A, B and C, repeated for D, E and F, and the section colours say the same (yellow L1-L2, blue L2-L3, orange L3-L1). PE runs to a ground symbol and joins no bus. Each section's output passes a second metering element (branch metering).

outlet-pitch.note: drawing - NOT DIMENSIONED, MEASURED FROM THE PATHS, as on the pilot: the 42 lamps stand at the 25.4 outlet pitch's alternation (27.8 then 23.0 apart, C13 to C39 and back), and A1's C13 recess starts at 198.33, 3.24 into its moulding, as 9001-22301's does.

photos.note: borrowed - THE GALLERY IS SHARED, NOT THIS SKU'S OWN. The EVMA8365X page lists four CHASSIS_424 masters (FRONT, BACK, SIDE, HRZ) and two EVMI8365X shots (the metered-input sibling on the same chassis: the brochure gives both 72 x 2.1 x 2.6 in, the CS8365, 42-outlet, 1829 mm build). CHASSIS_424_HRZ, a straight-on full length at 3000 px, shows six breakers A to F, which is this drawing and not the EVMI2130X's three, and is used as the second reading for the section colours, the labels and the outlet lamps. EVMA8365X_DT01 is byte-identical to EVMI2130X_DT06, an in-rack lifestyle shot, and is evidence of neither.

rear.note: drawing - the rear view of 9001-22312: the two mounting buttons on the width's centre line (the 1.02 [26.00] dimension), 124.00 from the cord end and 1555.8 apart (at 1679.8), and a 5.4 threaded hole 55.80 beyond each, at 179.8 and 1735.6, where the buttons can be moved. The view is symmetric about its centre line, so the rear is the view unmirrored.

relief.note: drawing - the side view puts the outlet mouldings 3.96 proud of the face and their lamps 5.0. The mouldings are drawn flat, as on the pilot (a raised box would bury the outlets placed on it in 3D); the lamps are domed 1.0, their height over the moulding. The outlets are wells, 18 and 20 deep, from their own contracts; the breaker plates are built 7.5 proud from theirs. The network module is 40 deep (estimated), inside the 65 mm body.

sections.note: drawing and photo - 9001-22312 labels SECTION A (YELLOW), B (BLUE), C (ORANGE), then the network module, then D (YELLOW), E (BLUE), F (ORANGE); CIRCUIT BREAKERS: (6) 20A 2-POLE LISTED, one plate at the head of each section with its letter on a tile in the section's colour. The outlets are printed A1-A7, B8-B14, C15-C21, D22-D28, E29-E35 and F36-F42: CHASSIS_424_HRZ reads all six strips so. THE DRAWING MISPRINTS SECTION F as F36, F37, F38, E39, E40, E41, E42; the photograph of the chassis reads F39 to F42, and every other strip on the sheet runs one letter, so the photograph is taken (gaps: section-f-labels).

sides.note: drawing - the side view of 9001-22312, the long side at the strip's edge (third angle, below the front view), which is the standing PDU's right; x = 0 is the face. Hex threaded inserts (6.35 across flats, drawn as a 6.6 disc as on the pilot) at 124.0, 179.8, 1679.8 and 1735.6, 20.0 behind the face (the 1.77 [45.00] dimension, from the back), the side-mount positions for the buttons; six Torx screws 6.0 across, 20.0 behind the face, at 32, 385, 728, 1091, 1449 and 1797; end-cap screws 6.0 across, 38.5 behind the face, 7.0 from each end; two screws 6.8 across 7.0 behind the face at 885.45 and 1049.9, at the ends of the module slot. A seam runs the length 13.2 to 14.8 behind the face.
